title: Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan

epigraph.quote: “All models are wrong, but some are useful.”
epigraph.author: George E. P. Box

book_paragraphs: An honest investment decision begins by steelmanning both sides of the aisle with the latest November 2026 facts rather than anchoring to a prior conviction. The bull case for TD Power Systems has real operational teeth. Following audited FY2026 revenue of ₹1,856 crore and net profit of ₹239 crore, H1 FY2027 revenue surged to ₹1,482 crore with 20.02% standalone EBITDA margins [1][2]. On the 13 November 2026 earnings call, management upgraded FY2027 revenue guidance from ₹2,600 crore to ₹2,900–₹3,000 crore and introduced FY2028 guidance of ₹3,400–₹3,500 crore [40]. Equally important, H1 FY2027 consolidated operating cash flow inflected sharply to ₹211.74 crore—roughly 101% of H1 PAT—answering the single biggest historical criticism from FY2026 [42].

The strategic bull case adds multi-year global OEM validation. On 19 November 2026, TDPS broke ground on a dedicated fourth manufacturing plant under its 10-year framework agreement with Siemens Energy to build 125–325 MW two-pole gas-turbine generators, targeting Q1 CY2028 readiness and 70–80% utilization by FY2030 [46]. Combined with more than 8,000 installed machines worldwide, low funded debt (0.00x D/E), and ₹675 crore of freshly raised equity capital, bulls argue that TDPS is graduating from a small Indian generator vendor into a scaled global supply-chain partner for data-centre and grid-reliability gas power [1][42][46].

The skeptic's case is equally grounded in hard disclosures—and directly explains why the stock is down 31.43% from its 52-week high. First, extreme export concentration (90–92% of H1 FY2027 inflows of ₹1,406 crore) collides head-on with cumulative 50% U.S. tariffs on Indian goods. Management's contingency plan to route partial assembly through Turkey (15% U.S. tariff rate) to secure a 'Made in Turkey' nameplate carries customs, rules-of-origin, and dual-site execution risks [44]. Second, the dedicated fourth plant is a build-to-print arrangement relying on Siemens Energy's intellectual property rather than TDPS's proprietary designs, involves 18–20 month execution cycles, commits capital ahead of binding purchase orders, and carries a management-flagged temporary EBITDA margin dip during ramp-up [46].

Third, the skeptic highlights working-capital and governance friction. Even as H1 CFO rebounded, standalone trade receivables jumped 35% in six months from ₹708.65 crore (March 2026) to ₹956.31 crore (September 2026), confirming that OEM credit terms remain generous [42]. Management has also stopped taking fresh railway orders and is winding down its Alstom/Indian Railways traction backlog (₹211 crore in June 2026 down to ₹170 crore in September 2026) [41]. Meanwhile, promoter shareholding fell from 34.27% in September 2024 to 26.51% post-QIP, the 12 November filing gave no itemized QIP proceeds-deployment schedule, and institutional holder Oxbow Capital Management cut its stake from 3.08% to 1.42% through 13 November 2026 [42][45].

We translate this clash of evidence into three explicit two-year (FY2028–FY2029) post-QIP scenarios. The Bear case (35% probability) values TDPS at ₹410 per share (₹11.70 diluted EPS at 35x P/E), reflecting U.S. tariff/Turkey routing delays, cyclical order normalization, elevated receivables, and multiple compression. The Base case (45% probability) values TDPS at ₹720 per share (explicit FY2029E diluted EPS of ₹16.00—an 8.5% step-up from FY2028E midpoint ₹14.75 EPS—at 45x P/E), trimmed from ₹820 to reflect post-QIP dilution, single-OEM build-to-print dependency, and tariff friction. The Bull case (20% probability) values TDPS at ₹990 per share (₹19.80 diluted EPS at 50x P/E), assuming tariff resolution, seamless fourth-plant ramp, and sustained ~100% CFO-to-PAT conversion. The probability-weighted fair value is ₹665.50 (~₹666), offering just +13.4% upside from the live 2026-11-25 close of ₹587.05 against -30.2% bear-case downside. Under a harsher 30x cyclical stress multiple, even full FY2028E midpoint delivery (₹14.75 EPS × 30x = ₹442.50) implies -24.6% downside, and Bear EPS (₹11.70 × 30x = ₹351.00) implies -40.2% downside.

Separating the three investment horizons resolves any confusion between a growing factory and a broken stock. For short-term trading and momentum, the verdict is REJECTED / AVOID. On the 2026-11-25 live snapshot, TDPS sits in confirmed Stage 4 (AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN, CAP_REJECTED), 11.12% below its 10-week EMA, 17.39% below its 50-day SMA, 11.84% below its 30-week SMA, and 2.37% below its 200-day SMA, with 7 distribution days in 25 sessions, -40.04% 28-day relative strength, and no 4-hour reversal. It has exited TheWrap Stage 2 list. Fighting institutional distribution in Stage 4 violates our core capital-preservation discipline.

For medium-term inflection (6–18 months), the verdict is CONDITIONAL WATCH. Upgraded FY2027 guidance (₹2,900–₹3,000 crore) and FY2028 guidance (₹3,400–₹3,500 crore) provide strong revenue visibility, and H1 CFO of ₹211.74 crore was encouraging [40][42]. However, the next two quarters must prove three things before medium-term conviction can return: U.S. shipments must navigate tariff and Turkey routing rules without customs disruption, standalone receivables must stop outgrowing sales, and management must publish a clear capital-deployment bridge for the ₹675 crore equity raise.

For long-term compounding (3–5+ years), the verdict remains POTENTIAL, NOT PROVEN (business quality: CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL; KPI health: PASS_WITH_WATCH). TDPS has earned impressive ROCE (34.0% on Screener) and deep global OEM trust, but build-to-print single-customer concentration at the fourth plant, cyclical capital-goods history, and historical cash-conversion volatility keep it short of a durable secular compounder. A true compounder proves that expansion capex earns high returns across cycles without requiring repeated equity dilution or working-capital stretch.

For new capital, our verdict is unequivocally REJECTED (Conviction Tier: TIER_0; Rejection Reasons: TREND and VALUATION). Both technical and valuation gates fail today. The chart is in a confirmed Stage 4 markdown (`CAP_REJECTED`), and at 54.2x–55.7x trailing earnings with a probability-weighted fair value of ₹666 against a ₹410 bear floor, there is no valuation margin of safety to justify catching a falling knife. Zero new capital is allocated. The ₹550–₹575 range shown in the execution table is strictly a historical 20-day swing-low reference shelf—not an active buy zone or limit order. Re-underwriting requires a completed Stage 1 base, a confirmed Stage 2 breakout above rising 50-day and 200-day averages, and verified tariff/receivables clarity.

For our existing Zerodha holding, the action shifts from HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP to EXIT_ON_BOUNCE (470 shares to sell). On the 2026-11-23 positions ledger (priced at ₹605.30 NSE close), the 470 shares carried a market value of ₹2,84,491.00 against a cost basis of ₹2,99,162.95 (average cost ₹636.52), an unrealized loss of -₹14,671.95 (-4.90%), and a 6.67% portfolio weight. At the live 2026-11-25 TradingView close of ₹587.05, market value is ₹2,75,913.50 and the unrealized loss widens to -₹23,249.45 (-7.77%). Holding a 6.67% tactical momentum position through a Stage 4 breakdown below the 200-day SMA with institutional selling and tariff overhang is unacceptable risk.

Why a tightened two-tranche EXIT_ON_BOUNCE rather than holding all 470 shares for ₹620? Because honest risk math forbids hoping for a bounce above broken resistance. Waiting for ₹620 against a ₹545 stop offers only +₹32.95 upside versus -₹42.05 downside (an unfavorable 0.78:1 ratio) while exposing a 6.67% portfolio weight to unhedged 6.56% daily ATR (₹38.53) gap risk. We therefore sell 235 shares (50%) immediately at market (~₹587.05) to halve Stage 4 exposure to ~3.3%, ratchet our hard stop upward from ₹520.00 to ₹545.00 (+4.8%, strictly below live CMP and the ₹557.05 swing low), and exit the remaining 235 shares into broken 200D/40W resistance (₹601–₹615, alert ₹605.00).

This tightened two-tranche plan cuts unhedged Stage 4 risk immediately without chasing an unrealistic bounce target. Selling 235 shares at ~₹587.05 locks in ~₹1.38 lakh of cash and halves dollar gap risk. On the residual 235 shares, exiting into ₹605–₹615 recovers +₹4,218 to +₹6,568 versus ₹587.05, while a confirmed daily close below ₹545.00 caps residual incremental downside at -7.16% (-₹9,882, or ~₹9,055 per 1-ATR gap) ahead of the ₹485 S2 pivot. Remember: these are advisory alerts, not live broker orders, and the ledger should be verified against live Zerodha holdings before execution.

Our capital redeployment plan is equally disciplined. Once the 470-share exit executes—freeing ~₹1.38 lakh immediately on 235 shares plus ~₹1.41–₹1.45 lakh on the residual 235 shares into ₹601–₹615—we allocate 100% of the proceeds (and any next marginal cash unit) to CASH, 0% to the active India shortlist, and 0% to outside candidates inside this single-company dossier. On the active India shortlist (`data/shortlist/IN.json`), Stage 2 compounders such as Coforge (ACCUMULATE_ON_DIP) and Zydus Lifesciences (ACCUMULATE_ON_DIP) sit in healthier technical structures, while broader India breadth remains narrow (48.2% above 200DMA). Retaining 100% in cash preserves optionality until the next portfolio-level audit deploys capital into a verified Stage 2 support pullback.

What evidence would force us to revisit this cautious verdict in future quarters? Four falsifiable checkpoints govern the re-underwriting trigger: first, Q3 and Q4 FY2027 revenue hitting ₹725–₹750 crore per quarter without margin erosion below 18.5%; second, audited FY2027 consolidated CFO staying above 85%–90% of PAT while standalone receivables stop growing faster than revenue; third, transparent disclosure of QIP proceeds deployment and clean U.S. customs clearance on Turkey-routed or India-shipped generators; and fourth, a repaired weekly chart reclaiming the 30-week SMA with rising relative strength. Until those facts align, discipline demands stepping aside.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The hardest skill in investing is respecting a broken chart even after management raises guidance. Good operational news that fails to lift a stock above its 200-day average is a warning about valuation, supply, or hidden risk. Sell half immediately, exit the rest into broken 200D/40W resistance, keep the ₹545 stop hard, and let cash wait for cleaner setups.
